text.title: Google Ads Campaign Setup Failure Modes
text.summary: 5 antipatterns observed in real deployments of Google Ads Campaign Setup — ENABLED on create, Display + Partners left on, under-built RSA, omitted network_settings, location name strings. Each pairs symptom + sourced root-cause + concrete fix.

antipattern.symptom: Campaign created ENABLED via API; conversion tracking not yet wired; smart bidding optimizes on zero conversions; budget burns in hours.
antipattern.fix: Default API call to status=PAUSED; flip to ENABLED only after checklist pass.

antipattern.symptom: API created Search campaign; Display + Partners active by default; CTR drops 50% due to display impressions; CPA inflated.
RSA with 5 headlines launched; Ad Strength: Poor; impression share 30% below target.
antipattern.fix: Require 15 headlines + 4 descriptions before save; reject ads under threshold.

antipattern.symptom: Omitting network_settings fields when creating a Search campaign via API.
antipattern.root-cause: API defaults enable Display Network and Search Partners. Agents that do not explicitly set target_content_network=False create campaigns that spend on irrelevant placements.
antipattern.fix: Set all three network flags explicitly on every create call (explicit-network-flags rule); the launch gate rejects a campaign whose network_settings block is absent.

antipattern.symptom: Using country or city name strings in location targeting criteria.
antipattern.root-cause: Location targeting only accepts geoTargetConstants/<numeric-id> format. Name strings fail validation with a non-obvious error that does not mention the format requirement.
antipattern.fix: Resolve every location to its geoTargetConstants/<id> via GeoTargetConstantService before building the criterion.
